current_round.prompt:
Implement the missing top-level refine config CLI command group for the active target app.

Behavior and scope:
- Make project configuration inspectable and mutable without curl or direct durable-state edits. Cover the configuration capabilities currently owned by GET/PATCH /api/settings, GET/PATCH /api/quality, GET/PATCH plus rule generation for /api/governance, and GET/PUT /api/guidance.
- Provide discoverable, scriptable subcommands for reading all configuration or one domain; applying validated ordinary settings patches; configuring Quality business requirements, instructions, and plain-text tests; configuring Governance product, constitution, automatic-round limit, rules, and rule generation; and listing, adding, editing, enabling/disabling, and removing Guidance entries.
- Support practical automation and multiline content through clear flags plus JSON and file or stdin input where appropriate. Emit stable pretty JSON on success and actionable structured errors on invalid input, missing active app, unreachable daemon, or server conflict. Mutations must return and display authoritative readback.
- Route normal operations through the checkout-owned local daemon with the current API contract version and idempotency behavior. Reuse the same services and validation as browser/API settings. Never direct-edit .git/refine-live-state or create a second configuration model.
- Preserve existing domain ownership: project attach/switch, workflow pause/resume, node and fleet management, Reporter/Todo lifecycle, and agent provider authentication remain in their established command groups. Document this boundary in help so config does not become an unstructured duplicate of every setting-related command.
- Avoid client-side lost-update races for Guidance or Governance list mutations. If item-level mutations require backend capability changes, implement them under the existing repository coordination and durable-state authority with stable item identity or another explicit conflict-safe contract; preserve unrelated entries and audit failures.
- Register the complete command tree in refine commands, handle explicit target-root test adapters consistently with other daemon-routed families, and keep CLI help concise and machine-discoverable.

Architecture and intent:
- Follow the existing src/surfaces/cli action and dispatch organization, thin daemon transport, shared API/service ownership, JSON-first output, detached-safe behavior, and local-first state model.
- Use the Goal plus relevant docs/intent pages for CLI, API, Settings, Guidance, Quality, Governance, and Target App. Update only affected intent documentation and any necessary command/runbook examples.

Verification and evidence:
- Add focused parsing, help, and command-catalog tests for every new subcommand and argument form.
- Add daemon-routing integration coverage proving reads and writes use shared endpoints, include API version and idempotency headers, preserve unrelated fields/items, and read back the saved result.
- Cover validation and failure paths: detached app, unreachable daemon, unknown settings, malformed JSON/file/stdin, invalid Quality or Governance values, missing Guidance entries, and concurrent or stale list mutation.
- Verify existing browser/API behavior remains semantically unchanged. Run focused exact Rust tests, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --all-targets, relevant CLI/web-server suites, and git diff --check; report exact commands and results.

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.
guidance_candidates.name: Intent and architecture
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
guidance_candidates.name: Cohesive code files
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

findings.description: The conflict-safe Guidance and Governance design does not include adapting the existing browser writers: Guidance rebuilds an edited item without preserving any identity and PUTs the entire list, while Governance autosave PATCHes the entire rules list without an expected revision. Leaving those compatibility routes unfenced still permits stale browser writes to erase concurrent CLI changes; making revisions mandatory without updating the browser instead breaks existing behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add browser and legacy-route work that preserves stable identities, carries an observed collection revision on every whole-list mutation, rejects stale writes with 409, refreshes after conflicts, and tests browser-versus-CLI races.

findings.description: No checklist item implements the requested verification: exhaustive parsing/help/catalog coverage, daemon-routing headers and readback, malformed input and detached/unreachable failures, preservation and stale-writer races, browser/API regression coverage, or the specified formatting, check, and suite commands.
findings.recommendation: Add a dedicated verification item enumerating the focused CLI, service, HTTP integration, concurrency, and browser compatibility tests plus every required cargo fmt, cargo check, relevant suite, exact-test, and git diff check command.

result.summary: Revise the plan to make all list-writing surfaces revision-aware and to include the required focused and regression verification.

checklist.description: Define a cohesive Config action hierarchy and dispatch boundary for all-domain and per-domain reads, Settings and Quality patches, Governance configuration and rule generation, and Guidance list, add, edit, enable, disable, and remove operations, with help that points project, workflow, node, fleet, Reporter, Todo, and agent-authentication concerns to their existing command groups.

Add a shared config input decoder for scalar and multiline flags plus mutually exclusive inline JSON, file, or stdin payloads, rejecting absent, overlapping, unknown, malformed, and domain-invalid input before daemon transport.

Register the complete Config tree in top-level dispatch and `refine commands`, route production requests through the checkout-owned daemon with the current API version and mutation idempotency contract, preserve the hidden explicit-target-root test adapter, and emit stable pretty JSON or structured detached, transport, validation, not-found, and conflict errors.

Refactor Guidance persistence into cohesive codec and mutation responsibilities that compatibly migrate existing entries to stable identities and collection revisions, then perform locked compare-and-set item and whole-list writes that preserve unrelated entries and return authoritative normalized state.

Extend Governance persistence under the existing durable authority with locked partial scalar updates, stable rule identities, an observed rules revision for every replacement or generated-rule adoption, and conflict-safe preservation of unrelated rules and fields.

Expose Guidance item mutations and revision-fenced Guidance and Governance whole-list compatibility writes through the existing API capability groups, returning explicit not-found and stale-revision conflicts while retaining current GET, PATCH, PUT, and rule-generation workflows.

Update browser Guidance editing and Governance autosave and generation to retain item identities, submit the observed collection revision on every list write, consume authoritative readback, and refresh visible state after a 409 instead of retrying stale content.

Keep ordinary Settings and Quality updates as partial mutations through their current services, so shared unknown-setting and domain validation remains authoritative, omitted values stay unchanged, and CLI output reflects the saved readback.

Update only the affected CLI, API, Settings, Guidance, Quality, Governance, and Target App intent pages and necessary examples to document daemon ownership, input and concurrency contracts, machine-readable readback, and the boundary with established command families.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P4 through P7 now require stable identities and observed collection revisions for item and whole-list writes, update browser and compatibility writers to preserve those values, reject stale writes with 409, and refresh after conflicts.

The requested focused coverage and gate commands remain mandatory implementation-phase evidence, but the authoritative Revise contract excludes verification and commands from this compact implementation checklist.

result.summary: Add a top-level `refine config` family that exposes Settings, Quality, Governance, and Guidance through the active checkout-owned daemon, with structured automation inputs, stable JSON readback, and shared validation, while strengthening Guidance and Governance collection contracts so CLI, browser, and compatibility writers cannot erase concurrent changes.

checklist.evidence: Added cohesive Config actions for all-domain/domain reads; Settings and Quality show/set; Governance show/set/generate-rules; and Guidance list/add/edit/enable/disable/remove. Top-level help explicitly keeps project, workflow, node, fleet, Reporter, Todo, and agent authentication in their existing groups.

Added one shared object decoder for scalar and multiline flags plus exclusive inline JSON, file, or stdin sources. Empty, overlapping, malformed, non-object, unknown, and domain-invalid inputs are rejected before mutation; focused decoder and CLI tests cover the forms and failures.

Registered Config in dispatch, hidden target-root detection, help, and the machine-readable command catalog. Production calls use daemon_json with X-Refine-API-Version and Idempotency-Key, successful responses are pretty JSON, config failures are structured JSON, and daemon integration tests assert routes, headers, request body, and authoritative readback.

Guidance codec now migrates legacy arrays to a revisioned document with stable entry ids. The service separates codec and locked mutations, supports item add/edit/remove, fences observed revisions, preserves unrelated entries, writes atomically, and returns normalized authoritative collections.

Governance load/save now run under the existing record lock, preserve omitted scalar fields and unrelated rules, assign stable rule ids, maintain rules_revision for replacements/generated adoption, reject unknown or invalid fields, and return authoritative normalized state.

Added POST /guidance and PATCH/DELETE /guidance/{id}; retained GET/PUT Guidance and GET/PATCH/generate Governance. Whole-list writes require the observed collection revision after migration, stale writes return 409, missing ids return 404, and API tests prove stale list writes preserve concurrent entries.

Browser Guidance editing now uses stable item routes and observed revision. Governance autosave submits rules_revision, applies authoritative ids/metadata/readback, and generated rules use that same save path. Both surfaces force-refresh on 409 instead of replaying stale state.

Settings still delegates partial patches to FileSettingsService and Quality to FileQualityService/QualitySettingsPatch. Omitted fields remain unchanged, unknown Quality fields are rejected, and direct adapter plus full API suites confirm authoritative saved readback and unchanged existing behavior.

Updated only affected CLI, API, browser Settings, Guidance, Quality, Governance, and Target App intent pages with daemon ownership, input/readback, revision conflict, stable identity, and command-family boundary contracts.

checklist.description: Define cohesive config action and dispatch modules with concise help and catalog entries for all-domain or single-domain reads, Settings patches, Quality updates, Governance updates and rule generation, and Guidance item lifecycle commands while explicitly excluding commands owned by other families.

Add one config input decoder that combines clear scalar and multiline flags with mutually exclusive inline JSON, file, or stdin sources and rejects missing, overlapping, unknown, or malformed values before transport.

Route production config operations only through the existing daemon transport with API-version and idempotency headers, aggregate domain reads into stable pretty JSON, map local and server failures to structured errors, and use authoritative post-mutation readback with the established hidden target-root test adapter.

Evolve Guidance normalization compatibly to assign stable item identities and revision metadata, then add record-locked item mutations with expected-revision checks so add, edit, enable, disable, and remove preserve unrelated entries and reject stale writers.

Extend Governance rule handling under the same durable authority with record locking, stable rule identities, revision-aware item changes, and conflict-safe adoption of generated rules while retaining product, constitution, and automatic-round-limit validation.

Expose the new Guidance and Governance item operations through their existing API capability groups with explicit not-found and conflict responses, while keeping current browser GET/PATCH/PUT behavior semantically compatible and backed by the same services.
Keep ordinary Settings and Quality mutations as partial patches through their current services so unknown settings and invalid Quality values fail consistently and omitted fields remain unchanged.

Update only the affected CLI, API, Settings, Guidance, Quality, Governance, and Target App intent text and necessary examples to document daemon authority, machine-readable configuration workflows, concurrency behavior, and the boundary with established command groups.

previous_rounds.prompt:
Implement the missing top-level refine config CLI command group for the active target app.

Behavior and scope:
- Make project configuration inspectable and mutable without curl or direct durable-state edits. Cover the configuration capabilities currently owned by GET/PATCH /api/settings, GET/PATCH /api/quality, GET/PATCH plus rule generation for /api/governance, and GET/PUT /api/guidance.
- Provide discoverable, scriptable subcommands for reading all configuration or one domain; applying validated ordinary settings patches; configuring Quality business requirements, instructions, and plain-text tests; configuring Governance product, constitution, automatic-round limit, rules, and rule generation; and listing, adding, editing, enabling/disabling, and removing Guidance entries.
- Support practical automation and multiline content through clear flags plus JSON and file or stdin input where appropriate. Emit stable pretty JSON on success and actionable structured errors on invalid input, missing active app, unreachable daemon, or server conflict. Mutations must return and display authoritative readback.
- Route normal operations through the checkout-owned local daemon with the current API contract version and idempotency behavior. Reuse the same services and validation as browser/API settings. Never direct-edit .git/refine-live-state or create a second configuration model.
- Preserve existing domain ownership: project attach/switch, workflow pause/resume, node and fleet management, Reporter/Todo lifecycle, and agent provider authentication remain in their established command groups. Document this boundary in help so config does not become an unstructured duplicate of every setting-related command.
- Avoid client-side lost-update races for Guidance or Governance list mutations. If item-level mutations require backend capability changes, implement them under the existing repository coordination and durable-state authority with stable item identity or another explicit conflict-safe contract; preserve unrelated entries and audit failures.
- Register the complete command tree in refine commands, handle explicit target-root test adapters consistently with other daemon-routed families, and keep CLI help concise and machine-discoverable.

Architecture and intent:
- Follow the existing src/surfaces/cli action and dispatch organization, thin daemon transport, shared API/service ownership, JSON-first output, detached-safe behavior, and local-first state model.
- Use the Goal plus relevant docs/intent pages for CLI, API, Settings, Guidance, Quality, Governance, and Target App. Update only affected intent documentation and any necessary command/runbook examples.

Verification and evidence:
- Add focused parsing, help, and command-catalog tests for every new subcommand and argument form.
- Add daemon-routing integration coverage proving reads and writes use shared endpoints, include API version and idempotency headers, preserve unrelated fields/items, and read back the saved result.
- Cover validation and failure paths: detached app, unreachable daemon, unknown settings, malformed JSON/file/stdin, invalid Quality or Governance values, missing Guidance entries, and concurrent or stale list mutation.
- Verify existing browser/API behavior remains semantically unchanged. Run focused exact Rust tests, cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo check --all-targets, relevant CLI/web-server suites, and git diff --check; report exact commands and results.
